findings.description: The unknown-task test depends on an approved set of supported task identifiers. CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of an unknown task, and CON-SUP-101 names the configured tasks, but neither identifies the complete supported set. The expected result for an identifier outside the default configuration is undefined.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved supported-task set and use it to select accepted and rejected identifiers for verification.

findings.description: Requiring the history to hold the eight most recent reports leaves older reports in scope for retention and leaves the expected history size undefined before eight faults occur. SYS-DIAG-008 returns the history contents, while CON-SUP-113 limits the service response to the last eight reports.
findings.requested_change: Specify which reports belong to the history exposed to the service tool when fewer than eight faults have occurred and when a new report displaces an older one.

findings.description: The item defines membership by detection, while SYS-DIAG-010 allows entry to occur later, before transmission starts. CON-SUP-110 requires history to survive software and watchdog resets. If a reset occurs after detection and before entry, the expected history contents are undefined.
findings.requested_change: Define when a detected fault becomes part of the retained history and whether a reset before entry changes the reports returned.

findings.description: The test must determine whether the start-up code integrity check correctly accepts or rejects the application image. STK-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-107 identify the image and when to check it, but provide no approved integrity criterion or reference for the expected verdict.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved image integrity criterion and reference information so tests can establish the expected outcome independently.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and the item identify the CRC-32 polynomial. The initialization, reflection and final XOR remain undefined. Different CRC values for the same configuration block can therefore satisfy the stated polynomial constraint, leaving the test without a unique expected value.
findings.requested_change: Reference the complete approved CRC-32 parameters for producing configuration blocks and verifying their stored CRC.

findings.description: Task release requires SYS-CFG-008 to have passed. SYS-CFG-008 defines positive fault-detection conditions only. With a valid block, the absence of a range fault does not establish that the range check has finished, so the release condition can be interpreted differently under CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-115.
findings.requested_change: Define a successful range-check outcome that establishes completion before the controller releases an application task.

findings.description: The 11 s limit applies to the duration of each pass but leaves the wait before the first pass and the gaps between passes unbounded. This permits long unchecked intervals even though CON-SUP-108 specifies processing a segment every control cycle and STK-SUP-008 requires repeated background checking.
findings.requested_change: Define when the first run-time pass starts and how successive passes continue, with a controlled reference to the CON-SUP-108 cadence.

findings.description: An 11 s scan can be timed, but the test cannot establish that it completed an integrity check. STK-SUP-008 requires the program-code check to be repeated. The approved image integrity criterion and reference needed to establish the expected result of a run-time pass remain open.
findings.requested_change: Identify the approved integrity criterion and reference for a full run-time pass, and verify its verdict as well as its duration.

findings.description: The required software reset request can be preempted by the window watchdog. For a flow fault at the end of a nominal 10 ms cycle, suppressing that cycle's refresh can leave about 2 ms before the CON-SUP-106 timeout. CON-SUP-110 requires the report and software reset sequence, but gives no precedence rule for this case.
findings.requested_change: Record the approved precedence and define the required reset outcome and deadline when watchdog expiry competes with the supervisor reset request.

findings.description: The instant at which all three signals are low is ambiguous if those signals were already low. For a start-up integrity fault, CON-SUP-109 holds them low from reset. The rationale uses the failing computation's completion as safe-state entry, but the statement does not identify that event as the reference for CON-SUP-110 ordering.
findings.requested_change: Tie the transmission start to safe-state entry for the particular fault and reference the start-up entry event defined by SYS-RST-012.

findings.description: The item adds an exclusive restriction, 'and from no other evidence.' CON-SUP-111 requires classification from the hardware flags but gives no basis for excluding corroborating evidence if the flags are insufficient to distinguish a supervisor reset from another reset.
findings.requested_change: Remove the exclusivity restriction or document its approved basis and show how flag-only classification supports all five classes.

findings.description: The proposed test sets reset-flag patterns and checks the resulting class. CON-SUP-111 names the classes but supplies no mapping or precedence for simultaneous or retained flags. The verifier cannot determine the expected class for those patterns.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved flag-to-class mapping and define how to handle simultaneous and retained flags in the classification test.

findings.description: This item requires a software reset request following a failed start-up computation. If a watchdog is active during the check, the time remaining after computation may be insufficient for the CON-SUP-110 report and reset sequence. The inputs give neither the start-up watchdog policy nor a bound on the check duration relative to expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve watchdog operation during start-up and establish the available time for the report and software reset request after a failing computation.

findings.description: The item requires transmission through the terminating line feed before the software reset request. A CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset can interrupt the report first once task-fault refreshes stop. CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112 leave the required report outcome in that case unresolved.
findings.requested_change: State the approved transmission outcome when hardware reset can preempt the report, including whether the full line must be sent and by what deadline.

findings.description: The hold applies 'while the controller is in the safe state,' which the SAFE-001 rationale defines by the output and status levels. A control output going high could itself make that condition false. The obligation needs a hold interval independent of the levels to verify the continued safe state required by STK-SUP-010.
findings.requested_change: Reference safe-state entry and permitted exit events that are independent of the output levels, including the exit condition for a latched safe state.

findings.description: The stated test must observe both outputs low from any reset. CON-SUP-005 identifies the simulator and CON-SUP-003 identifies GPIO, but neither establishes that the test can represent the board-level output during reset assertion and before software configures the pins.
findings.requested_change: Provide verification evidence for both output levels across the whole reset interval for each applicable reset path, and select a method that covers intervals outside the simulator's demonstrated capability.

findings.description: The stated test must observe the external status signal low from any reset, including a reset taken while it is high under SYS-SAFE-006. CON-SUP-003 and CON-SUP-005 provide no evidence that the test represents the status pin level before software can act.
findings.requested_change: Provide verification evidence for the external status level from reset assertion through software takeover for each applicable reset path.

findings.description: The fault-injection test calls for sampling both outputs from the preceding reset. A trace starting once the test build runs cannot establish the uninterrupted hold required by this item and CON-SUP-109 during reset assertion and early start-up.
findings.requested_change: Combine the start-up fault tests with evidence that covers both control output levels from reset assertion to the earliest observation supported by the tests.

findings.description: The proposed test samples the status signal from the preceding reset, but the reset-interval pin behavior is unresolved. An observation made after fault injection can show the low status required at detection and still miss an earlier high level prohibited by CON-SUP-109.
findings.requested_change: Verify the reset and pre-software interval as part of the uninterrupted status hold, alongside the start-up fault tests.

findings.description: The status signal's low level is part of the stated definition of safe state. Tying the hold only to that definition leaves the obligation unclear as soon as the signal goes high. The proposed test also stops at the next reset, although CON-SUP-110 permits only a power-on reset to clear a latched safe state.
findings.requested_change: Define the hold by independent entry and exit events and verify the latched status hold across software and watchdog resets.

findings.description: The item excludes a task period whose control cycle began before the checks passed. Its rationale assumes such a period cannot contain a scheduled release after the checks pass. CON-SUP-102 starts supervision when the checks pass, and CON-SUP-101 does not establish that alignment or the first T_DIAG release phase.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved start-up-to-schedule alignment to define the first counted window and the latest detection point for each task that never completes.

findings.description: The 100 µs deadline for detecting a late start is derived solely from the measurement resolution in CON-SUP-103. That resolution gives no bound on when the controller evaluates the comparison or declares the fault. CON-SUP-105 sets the origin of the safe-state budget.
findings.requested_change: Use a source-supported detection deadline or record the deadline as unresolved. State measurement resolution independently of detection latency.

findings.description: The proposed test infers a 100 µs detection deadline from the fault report. CON-SUP-112 and SYS-DIAG-005 specify a timestamp in milliseconds without approved sub-millisecond precision, and the report does not independently establish when the controller declared the fault.
findings.requested_change: Verify the approved deadline by observing the release, limit expiry and fault declaration on a time base with adequate precision.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 says an overrun is detected when the execution limit expires. The item waits for the measured value to exceed that limit and permits a further 100 µs. The stated derivation from measurement resolution does not authorize that delay.
findings.requested_change: Reconcile detection at expiry with the permitted completion exactly at the limit, and obtain approval for any allowed detection latency.

findings.description: The proposed test uses execution start plus the limit as a wall-clock expiry even though OP-SYS-013 leaves CPU time versus elapsed time unresolved. It then uses the CON-SUP-112 millisecond timestamp to judge a 100 µs deadline without a defined sub-millisecond format.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved execution-time measure to establish expiry and observe the actual overrun declaration with sufficient time resolution.

findings.description: The item combines the resolution of release-to-start measurement and the resolution of execution-time measurement. Either measurement can meet the CON-SUP-103 resolution while the other fails it, and the rationale already calls for separate exercises.
findings.requested_change: Make the resolution obligations for start delay and execution time independently traceable and judgeable.

findings.description: Testing only at the configured limit and 100 µs above it verifies two fault decisions. Both can be correct with a finer measurement resolution, although the item requires the exact 100 µs resolution specified by CON-SUP-103.
findings.requested_change: Verify the measured increments directly or use observations that distinguish the required granularity from finer and coarser measurements.

findings.description: The statement timestamps arrival when the task signals its checkpoint, while the rationale timestamps receipt by the supervisor. If a signal is issued before the cycle ends and received afterward, the two readings give different fault decisions under CON-SUP-104.
findings.requested_change: Define which event counts as arrival and how the end-of-cycle check treats a checkpoint at the boundary.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 requires checking the checkpoints of tasks released in that cycle, but the per-task event that produces a checkpoint and the expected number per release remain undefined. T_DIAG can execute for 20 ms under CON-SUP-103, so a completion checkpoint could arrive after its 10 ms release cycle despite compliant execution.
findings.requested_change: Specify the checkpoint event and count per release and define how to judge checkpoints that may arrive after their release cycle.

findings.description: The no-fault decision uses measured delay, but CON-SUP-103 and SYS-SUP-004 give only the 100 µs resolution. A start just after the configured limit can compare equal to the limit or greater than it, depending on how timestamps and configured values are represented.
findings.requested_change: Define or reference the time representation and comparison rule at the start limit, including how to handle times between measurement steps.

findings.description: For a preempted task, its own processor time can be within the CON-SUP-103 limit while elapsed time since execution began exceeds it. The item gives opposite expected fault outcomes depending on which quantity is measured.
findings.requested_change: Specify the execution-time measure and use it for the no-overrun boundary tests, including a preempted execution.

findings.description: The demonstration has no observable success criterion for 'run on the Renode simulator.' Loading the image, booting through the start-up checks and executing supervised cycles are different outcomes. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 require a usable environment for simulator-based verification.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable start-up and operational behavior that demonstrates the controller is running on the designated simulator platform.

findings.description: Refresh eligibility is fixed at the cycle boundary, but the refresh follows the flow check. An alive or timing fault detected after the boundary and before the refresh would leave this item requiring the refresh while SYS-WDG-005 forbids it. STK-SUP-005 permits servicing only while the tasks are healthy.
findings.requested_change: Make refresh eligibility cover the instant of actual refresh, while retaining the requirement to include the same cycle's flow check.

findings.description: The timeout is measured from a previous refresh. That gives no expiry reference if the watchdog becomes active and the first refresh never occurs. This case matters to the fallback reset required by STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Define when the window watchdog becomes active and what event starts the first expiry interval, or reference an approved start-up watchdog rule.

findings.description: The proposed test resets during transmission and then reads GET FAULTS. A report could enter the history after transmission starts but before the injected reset and still pass. That observation can verify survival of an interrupted CON-SUP-112 report, but cannot verify the item's required ordering.
findings.requested_change: Use a test that observes or brackets retained history entry and the first transmitted bit closely enough to detect entry after transmission starts.
